validation.rootTestsNote: Isolated host-root run: DSH_CONTROLS_HOST_ROOT plus the checksum-bound accepted tarball, so no environment-gated host integration case was skipped. A plain node --test without that host seam reports 789 cases with 288 environment-gated skips.
validation.featureEvidence: v0.4.17 keyed snapshot de-duplication by a per-prepare counter, and a live resumed PTC run showed the duplicate deliveries were unchanged: the session log records six identical 9.1 KB snapshots inside one step/start..step/end pair, before any nested dispatch, because the host assembles one admitted model request several times and every assembly called the pre-step hook again. Delivery is now keyed by the admitted step identity (turn:step) supplied by the host hook payload: an identical text is installed once per admitted step however many assembly passes or nested dispatches that step contains, a state change inside the step still delivers its new text, and a later admitted step re-offers the text whenever the host reports the exact baseline missing (rejected decisions, rewrites, spoofed copies, compaction, aborted attempts all covered by updated contract tests). The trade-off is explicit and documented: a message the host discards inside the same step is re-offered at the next step rather than again inside that step. The window command rejection now names reserve/release/reacquire and states that there is no read action, and the mattpocock_window description points T/S facts at the injected snapshot and mattpocock_history.

review.independentReview: none: the v0.4.17 fix was falsified by the live session's own injection counts after the restart (six identical snapshots still inside one step), which is what produced this corrected keying; the behaviour is locked by the per-step regression tests and the updated baseline-contract tests
